sections.voiceover: Milky Way estimates ranged from 500 billion to 2 trillion solar masses.

sections.voiceover: Researchers targeted 10,036 halo stars using the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument in Arizona. Didn't these halo stars extend up to 95 kiloparsecs from the Galactic center?
sections.visual_cue: Exterior shot of the Mayall Telescope dome atop Kitt Peak in Arizona, transitioning to high-tech spectrograph instrumentation.
sections.sfx_cue: Mechanical shutter click and subtle telescope swivel hum
b_roll: Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument focal plane graphic
sections.transition_out: Fade cut to astronomical grid display

sections.voiceover: But these 10,036 halo stars didn't stop until 95 kiloparsecs away.
sections.visual_cue: 3D galactic coordinate map plotting star positions stretching out into the distant stellar halo.
sections.transition_out: Match cut to Gaia orbital paths overlay

sections.voiceover: Astronomers combined Data Release 2 with space measurements from Gaia. This stellar survey narrowed the Milky Way's galactic weight.
sections.visual_cue: Dynamic animation merging DESI spectral data overlay with Gaia satellite stellar motion tracks, showing dark matter density contours.
sections.sfx_cue: Synthesizer swell resolving into clear crystalline resonance
sections.transition_out: Slow dissolve to wide Milky Way perspective

sections.voiceover: Astronomers now use Arizona's 4-meter Mayall Telescope to calculate the Milky Way's mass.
sections.visual_cue: Majestic wide shot of the spiral galaxy surrounded by its illuminated halo stars.
b_roll: Full Milky Way galaxy with halo stars highlighted
